newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: UN envoy returns to Kabul, to meet Taleban Rabbani.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy returns to Kabul, to meet Taleban Rabbani.

text.p: The United Nations' special envoy to Afghanistan, Norbert Holl, flew into Kabul on Wednesday for talks with Taleban leaders after meeting powerful warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum in the north.

Holl was due to meet Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, head of the six-man interim shura, or council, set up by the Islamic Taleban militia to govern the country after their takeover of the Afghan capital on Friday.
Asked if his talks with Dostum had done well, Holl would only say: "All my talks are good."

The U.N. is keen to avert a military confrontation between the Taleban and Dostum's forces, who are squaring off against each other at the Salang tunnel, about 90 kilometres (60 miles) north of Kabul.

Dostom's tanks, heavy artillery and multiple launch Grad missiles were dug in at both ends of the tunnel, which is part of the Salang highway that links Kabul and the north of the country and the former Soviet republics of Central Asia beyond.

Dostum, who controls large portions of northern Afghanistan, had previously managed to distance his forces from the fighting between the Taleban and the former Kabul government, which he also opposed.
Witnesses on the southern side of the frontline said it was calm on Wednesday and no fighting was reported.
